LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Pictured: Cam Ward, Joe Burrow. John Lanfranca Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:01 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) will host the Tennessee Titans (1-6) in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 13.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -950 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +640 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals pick: Bengals -13.5 (-110) My Bengals vs. Titans best bet is Cincinnati to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Titans vs Bengals NFL Odds Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +13.5 (-110), Titans -13.5 (-110) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-118o / 104u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +640, Bengals -950 Titans vs Bengals Preview for NFL Week 8 Tennessee Titans Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Cincinnati Bengals Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Picks, Betting Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. home.headline: Ja’Marr Chase’s absence from Bengals practice gets an explanation in latest injury report
home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The “rest” being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being “week-to-week.” Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) were also non-participants Wednesday in Nashville. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. picks.blurb: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Minnesota Vikings Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will attempt to notch two straight wins against NFC North divisional opponents when they take on the Minnesota Vikings. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players. The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams. Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field. Lions 23, Vikings 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions. The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week. Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league. I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays. picks.headline: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:25 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-0) own the longest active winning streak in the NFL. Dating back to November 30, 2025, they have won 11 games in a row, leaning on an exceptional defense and offense that emphasizes ball control. On Sunday, they head to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions (4-2), who have won two straight and are looking to stay within striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Lions' strengths are the opposite of the Vikings', ranking 2nd in scoring offense and yards per game through seven games, while no one is allowing more yards than Detroit. Minnesota's last four wins have come against teams with a combined record of 7-20. The Lions are the first opponent in a tough four-game stretch where the Vikings will play the Bills , Packers, and 49ers. Skeptics are waiting for Minnesota to come crashing back to Earth, and Sunday could be the first evidence of a regression if the Vikings' offense can't score some points. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings' matchup against the Lions. Kyler Murray will throw for over 300 yards One way you know you're making a bold prediction is if you can visualize people closing out of your article after reading. Minnesota's offense ranks 29th in passing yards. While Kyler Murray has avoided turnovers (two interceptions on 125 attempts), he hasn't consistently attacked defenses downfield. Kevin O'Connell said after last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts that the Vikings' offense is " not far off " from finding its footing. Four runs on the opening drive led to a turnover on downs, and a 3rd-and-5 on Minnesota's second drive ended in an incompletion when RG Will Fries pushed into Murray, who was ready to fire to a wide-open Justin Jefferson. Although the Vikings' defense has been elite since their 11-game winning streak began, O'Connell knows the offense will need to score to keep up with their next four opponents. Expect Murray to be less gunshy on Sunday, but here's hoping that doesn't result in recklessness. Murray goes for over 300, providing optimism moving forward that this passing attack can return to its pre-2025 self. The Vikings will intercept Jared Goff Like Murray, Lions QB Jared Goff has avoided turnovers this year. He has not thrown an interception through six games. However, Goff has still managed to complete 67.3% of his passes for 1,788 yards and 14 touchdowns for an offense that is tied for 4th-best in EPA/play. I'm not sure Minnesota can completely shut down this year's Goff, but they'll pressure him and force him into some bad plays. When the two teams last played, the Vikings forced Goff to turn the ball over five times (two interceptions, three fumbles). It may be difficult to replicate that production, but look for Brian Flores to flummox Goff into at least an extra possession. The Vikings will stop a fourth-down conversion Minnesota was somewhat susceptible to critical conversion attempts last week against Indianapolis. They allowed the Colts to convert 8-of-15 third-down attempts and their lone fourth-down attempt. Detroit converted 5-of-10 third-down attempts against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 but went 0-for-2 on fourth-down, including a controversial 4th-and-1 attempt from their own 24-yard line. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that fear of stopping the Packers' offense and gaining another possession played into last week's decision. I don't see him being nearly that aggressive from his own territory against the staunch Vikings defense. But I do think that this game will be close, forcing Campbell into a tough decision. Give me Flores' unit after they spent a week cleaning things up on the "weighty" downs. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8

Vikings Battle Will Be Won In the Trenches | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Sue Levine, Editor Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When the Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, this game will be won or lost in the trenches as Detroit's number-one offensive line goes head-to-head against the NFL's top-ranked defense. Earlier in the week, Dan Campbell described the Minnesota defense as good as it gets. " Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. Everything is fueled by this defense. That's the starting point." Over seven weeks this season, the Vikings' potent combination of LBs Blake Cashman and Andrew Van Ginkle, along with IDL Jalen Redmond, and EDGE Dallas Turner, led the league with an astounding 70.8 blitz rate . The Vikings' defense posted the league's highest pressure and sack rate, while allowing the lowest passer completion percentage in the NFL. Although Detroit boasts the NFL's second-highest scoring offense, averaging 30.66 points per game this season, the team faces a daunting challenge, taking on the mercurial Flores-designed defense. The Lions' success will depend on how well the newly re-configured offensive line can divert and delay the Vikings' punishing defense. Detroit Lions offensive tackle Blake Miller (76) and offensive lineman Tate Ratledge (69) block Arizona Cardinals defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (97) during the first half at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. The Challenge of Facing the Number 1 Ranked Defense Flores is one of the NFL's most enterprising defense coordinators who has earned a reputation for constantly changing things up to stymie opposing teams. His unpredictable Vikings defense forces multiple turnovers and generates mass confusion to limit the opposition's chances of scoring. The Minnesota defense in 2026 has held opposing offenses to an average of 12.33 points per game. The 5-2 Chicago Bears were held to a mere three points in Week 2, but the other teams the Vikings faced this season include the 1-5 Miami Dolphins, the 2-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2-5 New Orleans Saints, and the 2-5 Indianapolis Colts. The Vikings' defense has yet to face an offense comparable to the caliber of Detroit's high-powered offense. Dan Campbell remembers only too well how the Vikings' defense hurt the Lions a year ago. He admitted, "They did a hell of a job against us last year. They got after us. We turned the ball over, and we didn't make enough plays. They did, and we've got to play a hell of a lot better this year. That's the no-brainer statement there." "The Vikings defense understands how the system works," Campbell said, "and they use it to their advantage against the opposition." "They understand where they're going to exploit you at and then where you're trying to, 'OK, this is where my outlet is.' They take that away, too. They exploit you and then take away your outlet. They just create havoc and chaos. And inevitably, what they want, and have done consistently, is they force you to make massive errors…Turnovers, massive turnovers, so it's third-and-32. And that's where they want you, way behind the sticks." Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (83) carries the ball against Minnesota Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman (51) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images A Vastly Improved Detroit Lions Offensive Line Recognizing the Lions' disappointing 2025 season was largely due to a weakened, ineffective offensive line, Brad Holmes made rebuilding the offensive line his top priority. His smart, savvy acquisitions through free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft provided offensive line coach Hank Fraley with a significantly improved quality of offensive line talent. Holmes acquired versatile veteran lineman Juice Scruggs through the David Montgomery trade, signed free agent center Cade Mays, and drafted 2026 NFL Draft first-round pick, Blake Miller. The new trio joins All-Pro tackle Penei Sewell, Christian Mahogany, and Tate Ratledge to form the core of a newly reconfigured offensive line that could regain the success of previous years. Under Fraley's leadership in 2023 and 2024, the Lions' offensive line had been one of the NFL's best, ranked 2nd in the NFL with 8,864 rushing yards and 91 rushing touchdowns. In addition, Detroit's offensive line did an impressive job protecting Goff, and allowed the fourth fewest sacks (124) during that time span. Now, armed with the talent capable of producing similar results, the Lions are poised to knock the current NFC North division leaders off their top spot. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive line/ run game coordinator Hank Fraley against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Preseason Hiccups It takes time for a new offensive line to gel, and the Lions' preseason had its share of hiccups. Miller, the rookie right guard, cut his teeth going against All-Pro Aidan Hutchinson day after day. He got knocked down, pushed around, but to his credit, Miller got right back up, dusted himself off, and learned from his mistakes. Mays had been acquired to be the Lions' starting center, but after he fractured his wrist in the preseason, Scruggs stepped up and performed admirably. Through the first five weeks of the season, he earned a 75.6 PFF grade and ranked first among all 32 NFL centers. After the trials and tribulations of the 2025 season, Fraley once again has a group of talented players who can rise to the challenge of taking on the NFL's top defenses. However, this will be the o-line's biggest test to date. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70) prepares to snap the ball to quarterback Jared Goff (16) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images It All Starts With the Lions' Offensive Line Recently, Detroit's MVP candidate quarterback, Jared Goff, was asked how much he credits his success to the Lions' offensive line. Goff responded , "Oh, a ton. All of it. We can't do anything without those guys. We do have a really good skill group here, but they know, and we know as an offense, and as a team, we only go where they go. And so when they're playing well, we can do some pretty special things, and they know that." Coach Campbell agrees. However, as excited as he is already about the success of the Lions' offensive line this season, he expects we'll continue to see improvement ."But man, there are some things we are definitely getting better at. I'm excited about this O-line playing together. I mentioned this before, but now that we've kind of got those guys going here, we can get this five settled in and let them just soak them with reps together in real games and let them grow." The Last Word Sunday's game will undoubtedly come down to a ferocious battle in the trenches as the Minnesota defense does its best to pressure Goff, who holds the leagues-second highest passer rating of 112.5. Goff also leads the NFL with 14 passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown with zero interceptions over 1,788 passing yards. Last year, despite the limitations of the Lions' offensive line, Goff attained the elite production of over 4,500 passing yards. With the significantly improved coverage of Detroit's offensive line and the dual-headed threat posed by premier running back Jahmyr Gibbs, the majority of experts predict that Minnesota's talented defense will be in for a long and frustrating afternoon. Not everyone is believing in them despite the fast start. It feels like league-wide trend over the past week has been to pick against the Vikings. With Minnesota still unable to generate much in the way of offense many doubt their legitimacy as NFC contenders. One major newspaper seemed to continue that trend. All of their analysts chose for the Lions to surprise the Vikings and hand Minnesota its first loss of the year. Four NFL analysts from The Tennessean discussed who they would pick in the game between the Vikings and Lions. All four picked the Lions. Here's what one analyst , Bob Wojnowski, had to say about the matchup. "The Vikings are a homely 6-0, but unbeaten, nevertheless. Brian Flores' attacking defense stuffed the Lions last year with 10 sacks in two games. But behind a rebuilt, developing offensive line, Jared Goff is better equipped to handle it. Expect more than a few checkdowns throws to Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown, and another 25 carries or so by Gibbs. The Lions likely won't need to score a lot, which is good, because the Vikings allow only 12.3 ppg, tops in the league. The Lions' defense is coming off its best effort and can't let Minnesota's sluggish offense get untracked. Kyler Murray only has three TD passes and been sacked 12 times, but he's the Vikings' second-leading rusher. The Lions have to keep Murray in the pocket and can't let star receiver Justin Jefferson get free. Jefferson has only 23 catches and three touchdowns all season but he's gonna break out eventually. That's a tall ask if you have watched the team so far this season. Minnesota could more reasonably become an average offense. If they can, it's not hard to imagine a playoff run in the Vikings' future, especially given how little offense has been required to get to 6-0. Many have wondered how long it will take Murray to begin making star wide receiver Justin Jefferson a focal point in the offense. The Vikings are hoping to answer that question on Sunday. Jefferson will hope to lift the lid off the Vikings' offensive ceiling when Minnesota takes on Detroit.

away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Otherwise, almost all upgrades for the Lions on Thursday, with only starting cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. limited. Still, the Lions are shaky at cornerback and if Rakestraw can’t go that would be a notable loss. For the Vikings, upgrades across the board compared to Wednesday, with only Aaron Jones limited. A new addition, however, as Gavin Bartholomew did not practice with an ankle injury. Unclear if that will be something that keeps him out on Sunday or not. home.blurb: He was transported to a local hospital, the team announced . On Monday, the Lions updated Campbell's condition, saying preliminary indications "are positive," but noted that "out of respect for Jack and his family" they would not share further information on his injury. Head coach Dan Campbell provided a limited update after the game: Needless to say, losing Campbell would be a significant blow to the Lions, who are 5-2 and looking to return to the playoffs after missing the playoffs last season. Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered what appears to be a serious injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. After making a tackle, Campbell was unable to get up on his own power and received attention from medical staff on the field before being carted off. Simmons Makes Bears Even Stronger 😤 Jack Campbell is one of the most important pieces of the Lions' defense, coming into Sunday's game leading the team in total tackles (54). He added three more tackles against the Vikings on Sunday before suffering his neck injury. He's coming off a season in which he earned a First-team All-Pro nod after collecting a career-high 176 tackles, five sacks and three forced fumbles. Detroit rewarded Campbell for his career season by giving him a four-year, $81 million contract extension over the offseason. The Lions selected Campbell with the 18th overall pick in 2023 after his standout career at Iowa. The 26-year-old has since developed not only into one of the best linebackers in the league, but also into the leader of Detroit's defense. "This is Jack Campbell's defense, and I don't hesitate when I say that," defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said of Campbell earlier this year. "This is Jack Campbell's defense and everyone in that locker room knows it. Point blank period. picks.blurb: Raiders vs Jets game picks: Who the staff has winning Week 8 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Raiders vs Jets game picks: Who the staff has winning Week 8 matchup Levi Damien, Marvin Uzor, Lance Fernandez and LaMarr Fields, Raiders Wire Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week the Raiders head to the Meadowlands in New Jersey to face the New York Jets. Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. Across the picks rounded up here, the Raiders hold a 12-10 edge over the New York Jets , which is hardly a ringing endorsement for either side. Believe it or not, the loudest vote of confidence in Las Vegas comes from the Jets' own backyard. The Raiders Wire staff leans Las Vegas again, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 22-20. NFL.com tips toward the Raiders Three of the five NFL.com analysts picked the Raiders, with Gennaro Filice at 21-17, Bobby Kownack at 21-20 and Dan Parr at 24-23. Brooke Cersosimo went with the Jets 22-20, and Jeremy Bergman took New York 19-14 while sounding unimpressed by everybody involved. "These are two 3-5 teams in the making, solid rosters without winning instincts." Pete Prisco sees a lopsided Sunday Nobody in this roundup is lower on the Raiders than CBS Sports' Pete Prisco, who has the Jets winning 27-16. He believes defenses have figured out how to rattle the veteran quarterback. "Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks." His colleague Tyler Sullivan disagrees, taking the Raiders 24-21 and plus the points. ESPN and Bleacher Report lean New York ESPN's panel went 2-1 for the Jets, with Rich Maldonado at 24-20 and Eric Moody at 26-23, while Seth Walder has the Raiders winning 24-20. Maldonado expects New York to keep running the ball right at the Raiders' defense. ESPN's Football Power Index barely disagrees with its own experts, giving the Raiders a 52% chance to win. Bleacher Report's panel split 4-3 for New York straight up, with Gary Davenport, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski on the Raiders' side. Maurice Moton, who picked the Jets, summed up the stakes in one line. "Both of these teams are desperate for a win." The Jets' own backyard likes the Raiders As it turns out, the Raiders' biggest fan club this week sits in New Jersey. Four of the five Jets writers in the USA TODAY Network's Northeast group picked Las Vegas. Bob Jordan of the Asbury Park Press went 30-17, and Bert Bainbridge of NorthJersey.com went 30-20. Brian Marron also picked the Raiders, 27-17. Dave Rivera had the Raiders 23-20, and his reasoning stung for Jets fans. "The Jets weren't able to take care of business against the winless Dolphins team last week." Only Mike Dougherty of lohud.com sided with the home team, taking the Jets 27-24. All told, 10 of the 15 score predictions here land within four points, so a nail-biter feels like the safest call on the board. away.headline: New York Jets Rule Out T'Vondre Sweat for Las Vegas Raiders Game, List David Bailey as Doubtful
away.blurb: Officially ruled out are massive defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat and edge Joseph Ossai. On the cusp of being officially declared out is edge David Bailey, who has missed all three practices this week with a groin injury. He is listed as doubtful on the injury report, and his absence would be a big blow to any Jets hopes of taking down the Raiders. Linemen Darrell Jackson Jr., Nate Lynn and Harrison Phillips will be asked to step into the breach on defense for the Jets. Lynn had a sack against Miami (his first, along with his first NFL tackle), while Jackson has done well in limited appearances. Phillips, who has played for the Vikings and the Bills, has been less successful. His PFF grade is an abysmal 49.2, ranking 102 out of 126 qualified linemen. But he is a big body and will have to step up in the absence of Sweat, who has been a rock in the middle for the Jets. Listed as questionable is running back Breece Hall, who has been out since Week 3 with a quad injury. He was limited during this week’s practices. “He’s a key cog of what we’re doing,” head coach Aaron Glenn said of Hall. “And each time he goes out [and practices], man, there are certain points that he has to hit to make sure that we’re all good and we want to make sure we hit those points.” If Hall plays – a game-time decision – he will likely see limited action and share the backfield with Allen, who has been the No. 2 rusher in the NFL for the time period he’s taken over from Hall as the lead back. Left guard Dylan Parham was given a surprisingly good injury update. He fully participated in practice on Friday and will likely see at least spot duty. He’s been out with a knee injury since Week 3 against Detroit, but was playing as well as any Jets lineman when he went down. The New York Jets will be severely depleted on the defensive line for their Sunday game against the Las Vegas Raiders. The injury news on the other side of the ball is a bit brighter for the Jets. Running back Braelon Allen has been cleared after fully practicing on Thursday and Friday. Allen had a minor ankle injury sustained in the Miami game. The Raiders have a much better health situation than the Jets. The only definite scratch was edge Patrick Johnson. Tight end Brock Bowers practiced fully this week, a big plus for the Raiders, who often use two tight ends.

The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chris Pokorny Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the Pittsburgh Steelers this Sunday. Both teams enter with the same record, but Cleveland has the division edge after beating Pittsburgh on Thursday Night Football earlier this season. The Steelers are undefeated at home, so are they looking to give medicine back to the Browns? Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 8 game between the Browns and Steelers: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Steelers: In their first meeting, the Browns' defense controlled the line of scrimmage, sacking Aaron Rodgers five times while piling up 10 total QB hits and keeping the veteran signal-caller all out of sorts. Things have turned a corner for the Steelers' offense in the last three weeks, with Rodgers playing in rhythm, limiting the giveaways and accurately finding his targets — though there's still a lot of pressure on rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor, who allowed two sacks and seven pressures (per NGS) against the Browns in Week 4. Everything about the 42-year-old quarterback's play has trended upward since their last meeting, and the rushing attack should flex its muscle more this time around with the return of Rico Dowdle. The Browns have rightfully earned their place at the top of the division through two months, but how long can they end up on the winning side of close games? We've seen this type of playing-with-fire approach before, and it rarely lasts. That said, watching this team get meaningful contributions from young players (Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, Spencer Fano, Carson Schwesinger) has been enjoyable and should keep Cleveland competitive should they maintain that level. But this Sunday, playing the steadily improving, veteran-laden Steelers within confines of Acrisure Stadium could be the Browns' toughest matchup to date. Pittsburgh improves to 4-0 at home and takes over first place in the AFC North at midseason. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Steelers 24, Browns 20 This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 23, Steelers 20 The Browns have already beaten the Steelers once this season, and if they win this game, that would give them their first season sweep of Pittsburgh since 1988. That's right, it has somehow been 38 years since the Browns have swept the Steelers. The NFL should have flexed this game to Sunday night and asked everyone at the stadium to dress up like their favorite character from 1988. I would have definitely been John McClane from Die Hard, or maybe AC Slater. You know what? I'm not sure and we don't have time to talk about this. … (read more on CBS) Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Steelers 24, Browns 20 The Browns have all their five wins thanks to Deshaun Watson snatching victory from the jaws of defeat late in the fourth quarter. That's a feel-good development for rookie coach Todd Monken, but not sustainable as a first-place team. Aaron Rodgers is feeling it since the last Cleveland matchup and will outduel Watson with superior weapons. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Steelers 23, Browns 16 The Browns are 5-1 in one-score games – and their last six games have been decided by six points or less. Cleveland beat Pittsburgh in the first matchup, too. This time, Pittsburgh will build off the running game. The Steelers are 3-0 S/U at home, and Aaron Rodgers has a 101.6 passer rating.
