picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game Curt Popejoy, Steelers Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns square off, both teams at 5-2 and tied on top in the AFC North. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. Final score prediction: Steelers 35, Browns 24 This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game

picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . away.blurb: 3 Browns are questionable as team works out five players ahead of Week 8 According to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi , the Browns worked out five players ahead of the weekend: tackle Blake Austin, guard C.J. Hanson, center Jacob Rizy, and wide receivers Xavier Weaver and Brady Boyd. Head coach Todd Monken did not rule Howard out, however. He was listed as questionable for Week 8 along with defensive back Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas. 2 ruled out, 1 questionable for Steelers who enter this game close to full health The Steelers are healthy as well. They ruled out a pair of depth defensive backs in Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter on Friday. Both players have mostly played on special teams for Pittsburgh. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek is questionable for Sunday with a calf injury. He’s only been targeted four times by Aaron Rodgers in five game appearances this season. Can the Browns figure out how to score in the first quarter? The Steelers enter this game allowing 4.3 points per game in the first quarter. They should be able to put the Browns’ most maddening trend to the test out of the gate. Cleveland played man-to-man on Pittsburgh’s receivers on over 70% of Rodgers’ dropbacks in Week 4. The Steelers’ inability to create quick separation, and Rodgers’ propensity to get the ball out quickly, led to a 55% completion percentage and a lot of failed drives. The Browns are becoming a bad matchup for the Steelers, and that’s why we have them grinding out another close win. Watson has been getting the ball out quicker and making sounder decisions. Cleveland has the personnel, like tight end Harold Fannin, wide receiver KC Concepcion, and running back Dylan Sampson, to turn quick passes into big gains, limiting Pittsburgh’s elite pass rush. This game could easily go the Steelers’ way if the Browns struggle with sacks and turnovers. But if they can protect the football and get it out quickly, they should be in position to win it in the fourth quarter. Week 8 is dripping with opportunity for the Cleveland Browns. This is the spot, playing in a stadium that’s been a house of horrors for decades, that turns a feel-good start to the season into something much more real. The Browns are as healthy as they’ve been all season and are playing their best football, at least in terms of stringing together all three phases. A win over Pittsburgh would clinch their first regular-season sweep in the rivalry since the 1980s and would vault their record to 6-2 atop the AFC North. Browns fans have been craving meaningful football. It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh. From the key matchups to the injury concerns and everything in between, here’s a primer for one of the biggest games on this week’s slate. home.headline: Browns inactives, injury updates and keys to completing season sweep of Steelers
home.blurb: 3 Browns are questionable as team works out five players ahead of Week 8 According to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi , the Browns worked out five players ahead of the weekend: tackle Blake Austin, guard C.J. Hanson, center Jacob Rizy, and wide receivers Xavier Weaver and Brady Boyd. Head coach Todd Monken did not rule Howard out, however. He was listed as questionable for Week 8 along with defensive back Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas. 2 ruled out, 1 questionable for Steelers who enter this game close to full health The Steelers are healthy as well. They ruled out a pair of depth defensive backs in Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter on Friday. Both players have mostly played on special teams for Pittsburgh. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek is questionable for Sunday with a calf injury. He’s only been targeted four times by Aaron Rodgers in five game appearances this season. Can the Browns figure out how to score in the first quarter? The Steelers enter this game allowing 4.3 points per game in the first quarter. They should be able to put the Browns’ most maddening trend to the test out of the gate. Cleveland played man-to-man on Pittsburgh’s receivers on over 70% of Rodgers’ dropbacks in Week 4. The Steelers’ inability to create quick separation, and Rodgers’ propensity to get the ball out quickly, led to a 55% completion percentage and a lot of failed drives. The Browns are becoming a bad matchup for the Steelers, and that’s why we have them grinding out another close win. Watson has been getting the ball out quicker and making sounder decisions. Cleveland has the personnel, like tight end Harold Fannin, wide receiver KC Concepcion, and running back Dylan Sampson, to turn quick passes into big gains, limiting Pittsburgh’s elite pass rush. This game could easily go the Steelers’ way if the Browns struggle with sacks and turnovers. But if they can protect the football and get it out quickly, they should be in position to win it in the fourth quarter. Week 8 is dripping with opportunity for the Cleveland Browns. This is the spot, playing in a stadium that’s been a house of horrors for decades, that turns a feel-good start to the season into something much more real. The Browns are as healthy as they’ve been all season and are playing their best football, at least in terms of stringing together all three phases. A win over Pittsburgh would clinch their first regular-season sweep in the rivalry since the 1980s and would vault their record to 6-2 atop the AFC North. Browns fans have been craving meaningful football. It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh. From the key matchups to the injury concerns and everything in between, here’s a primer for one of the biggest games on this week’s slate. picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit. Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. The remaining questionable players include wide receivers Beaux Collins (hip) and Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), defensive ends Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Charles Snowden (back), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels stepped into a larger role against the 49ers and delivered one of the biggest performances of his young career. Daniels helped seal the victory with a late interception of Brock Purdy. Atlanta will need as many healthy players as possible against a Tampa Bay team coming off a convincing 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s matchup looking to build on that performance, while the Falcons are coming off a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated 49ers. Atlanta and Tampa Bay will meet Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. Meanwhile, Atlanta saw several players return to practice Thursday. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) were both upgraded to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith also returned in a limited capacity after receiving a rest day Wednesday. Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) remained the Falcons' lone non-participant Thursday due to injury. Atlanta continued to have several players limited, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). home.blurb: Backup running back Brian Robinson Jr. had already missed Week Seven against the San Francisco 49ers with a hamstring injury. That injury lingers, and he is out this week. Khalil Herbert will continue to back up starting running back Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was downgraded to out with a hamstring injury. With veteran safety Jessie Bates III , veteran defensive back Sydney Brown, and young safety Xavier Watts making the middle of the field a tough place to play for opposing offenses, Bowman Jr. has enough reinforcements to heal. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out again with a foot injury. Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been a one-two punch for Tampa this year, with almost identical stats. The main difference is that Egbuka has the touchdowns, with two this season. We will see how much that affects Tampa's offense on Sunday. Backup running back Kenny Gainwell and offensive tackle Luke Goedeke are both questionable and could also miss Sunday's game, hindering the offense. Last week's game plan was to lean on the run game, which will be harder without the backup running back and with an offensive lineman out. On paper, the Falcons have the advantage heading into Sunday's game. But you never know how these things play out. It bodes well for the Falcons to take advantage and win on Sunday, as it would give them control of the NFC South. Erickson Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 5:23 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts have made several roster changes due to injuries, particularly at cornerback and linebacker. Rookie linebacker CJ Allen is expected to start after recovering from an ankle injury, leading to the release of veteran Germaine Pratt. Cornerback Sauce Gardner returned to full practice, offering a potential solution to injuries in the secondary. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have made a flurry of roster moves this week, trying to cover a rash of injuries at the cornerback position while shoring up depth at linebacker. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen was a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day after missing last week’s game due to an ankle injury, although his fellow rookie, Bryce Boettcher, missed his second consecutive day with a groin injury. Indianapolis feels confident enough in its linebacker group to release veteran Germaine Pratt, who was signed to the practice squad two weeks ago but no longer has a path to playing time. Pratt played 20 snaps against Minnesota this week due to injuries, but the Colts plan to move Allen into the starting lineup now that he’s healthy. Pratt was a starter for 12 games in Indianapolis in 2025; the Colts are trying to get younger and faster at the position. “C.J. was going to start this week before he had that injury,” defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said. “I think they’re all putting their time in, and the more at bats they get, the better they’re going to be.” The Colts have larger issues at cornerback. Sauce Gardner practiced in full for the first time since suffering a calf injury against Tennessee, offering a potential starting option. Indianapolis placed Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve earlier this week, and Justin Walley missed the second consecutive day with a knee injury. OUT: Jaguars' DaVon Hamilton will miss rest of '26 with torn quad, Coen says Jacksonville Jaguars safety Eric Murray will miss the rest of the season with an elbow injury he sustained on the opening kickoff of Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts . Murray is the latest Jaguar to suffer a season-ending injury, after the team lost left tackle Anton Harrison for the year with a torn ACL while overseas in London. Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton also suffered a torn quad in Sunday's contest against the Colts. All three players will not suit up again for Jacksonville this year. Murray, 32, signed with Jacksonville via free agency ahead of last season and played in and started 12 games. He missed several games last year due to a neck injury. This year, Murray has played in six games (five starts), including Sunday's matchup against the Colts. Murray missed the team's Week 5 game against the Philadelphia Eagles while in the concussion protocol. Murray has accounted for 10 solo tackles this season. Through 17 starts with the Jaguars , Murray has totaled 69 tackles (42 solos), six pass breakups, one interception and one forced fumble. The Jaguars will turn to backups Rayuan Lane and Kaevon Merriweather to replace Murray. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.blurb: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Bears beat Seahawks College hoops takeaways Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday in their first meeting since the 2022 season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday's game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn't participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington's back locked up in practice, which is why he'll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers' side, they'll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. Replicating that performance is going to be much easier said than done in the rematch, however, especially with Andy Reid's team hitting the road. Denver seems to be finding its stride just a little bit, although a win over the Arizona Cardinals won't convince anyone that the reigning division champions are all the way back. The winner of Sunday's tilt could generate some serious momentum in the AFC West race as the season approaches its midpoint. What gives in the afternoon window of play? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 8 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: For the second week in a row, I'm expecting a low-scoring game. This time, however, I think the Chiefs will find the end zone. Kansas City just needs enough from Rashee Rice and his fellow pass catchers to allow Kenneth Walker to have opportunities similar to the ones he took advantage of in Week 1. The final inactives list will be massive for both teams, but I expect the Chiefs to escape Denver with a narrow win. Jordan Foote: Getting wideout Rashee Rice back in the fold for this one is huge. Given that Xavier Worthy's come back down to earth, Travis Kelce is banged up and Kenneth Walker III has finally looked human, having a formidable weapon on offense is paramount. On the other side of the ball, missing cornerback Mansoor Delane will hurt, but being minus L'Jarius Sneed might just be an addition-by-subtraction scenario. Expect a one-score game that is far from the prettiest, albeit with Kansas City still doing enough to complete the sweep of Denver and maintain first place in the AFC West. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are reeling after an ugly loss to Seattle in prime time last week. It’s difficult to imagine the offense looking any more inept than it did a week ago when it mustered just one field goal all night. The Broncos’ defense isn’t quite as dominant as Seattle’s but still is a formidable unit. With that said, we saw who the better team was when these two sides met in Week 1. Denver has been winning in spite of Bo Nix’s play, not because of it, and the KC coaching staff has to have stressed the importance of a game in which it could lose the first-place lead in the AFC West. Tyler Brown: This feels like a tighter game than Week 1, but the Chiefs' strengths match up well against those of the Broncos. Denver will be desperate with the divisional stakes swinging so heavily. With Jonathan Cooper lined up opposite Nik Bonitto, the Broncos have a better edge-rush pairing than they did in September, which puts the Chiefs’ tackle situation under real stress if it ends up in too many obvious dropback situations. The Broncos may perform better this go-around, but the matchup tilts toward the Chiefs. Denver’s rushing defense ranks 28th and leads the league in missed tackles, which is exactly the situation Kenneth Walker thrives in. Getting Rashee Rice back is a bigger deal than it may sound, because it gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable weapon and it lets Xavier Worthy and the rest of the group settle into their roles. On the other side, Denver is 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, and Nix has struggled when pressured, especially against the blitz. If Steve Spagnuolo gets creative and some pass rushers outside of George Karlaftis step up, that is another major Chiefs advantage. Fresh off a bad loss in Seattle, where they were thoroughly outclassed, the Chiefs are looking to show the world that game was a mirage. This game presents a huge opportunity for them to do just that. The Broncos have won three straight games following a 2-2 start to the season. Their offense has struggled for most of the year, but Sean Payton's team is finding ways to win. They have a chance to prove they're for real. With so much on the line, it's time to predict who comes out on top in this clash of AFC West rivals. Here's my official prediction for Chiefs vs. Broncos. Chiefs vs. Broncos Official Score Prediction This is a hard game to predict. Up until last week, the Chiefs looked like a Super Bowl contender. The offense was humming, and the defense was playing like an elite unit, despite some flaws. And then the Seahawks game happened. Kansas City played poorly, and all their flaws were exposed in 60 minutes of football. Now they have to hit the road again to play in another difficult road environment. The Broncos have revenge on their minds following a lopsided defeat to Kansas City in Week 1. Couple that with an offense maybe showing signs of breaking out and an elite defense, and this gets tricky for the visitors. There are a few things going in the Chiefs' favor. One, they can't possibly play worse than they did last weekend. Two, Kenneth Walker III usually doesn't stay down for long. He's due for a huge bounce-back performance. Denver's passing offense hasn't found consistency yet, but Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle (if he plays) should have more favorable matchups today. Ultimately, this is a tough spot in the schedule for Kansas City. They're banged up, coming off a terrible performance, and now have to play in Denver. Mahomes and Walker will bounce back and make a few plays against a great defense. But the injuries and lack of pass rush finally catch up to the defense. The Chiefs battle, but fall short and lose their grip on the AFC West. Broncos 24, Chiefs 20

away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. away.headline: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 Final injury report: Rashee Rice returning
away.blurb: Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) was listed as questionable after suddenly missing practice Thursday and Friday. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that it is the same shoulder he has dealt with injuries to since training camp and forced him to miss time in Weeks 1 and 2. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was listed as questionable after limited participation in practice for two days and missing on Wednesday with an NIR/personal designation. He is regularly listed as a limited participant due to a lingering knee issue. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was ruled out after three days of limited participation in practice; he was designated to return from the Physically Unable to Perform list on Wednesday . He will continue working in the 21-day practice window before the Chiefs must sign him to the active 53-man roster. Defensive end R Mason Thomas (personal) was listed as questionable after missing practice on Friday. On Friday, Andy Reid said Thomas will meet the Chiefs in Denver and will likely play. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) did not have a game status listed after improving to full participation in practice on Friday; he hasn’t played since tweaking his hamstring in Week 4, but he should be making his return to the field in Denver. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) did not have a game status listed and practiced in full on Friday after being labeled a limited participant in practice on Thursday. He banged up his ankle in the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was ruled out after missing practice all week; he hasn’t played since leaving the Week 5 win over the Los Angeles Chargers with an ankle injury. This season, he is tied for the team lead with two interceptions — one he returned for a touchdown — and has three passes defended, one forced fumble and three tackles for loss. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) was listed as questionable after limited practice on Thursday and Friday; he suffered his injury in the Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals . Pro Bowl defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) was listed as questionable after two limited practices to end the week following an absence from Wednesday’s practice. Allen has 4.5 sacks this year and hasn’t missed any time for this injury so far. away.headline: Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns
away.blurb: The Chiefs downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury, and the Chiefs have also placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve, according a report from Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk and multiple other outlets. Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns Bob McCullough Sun, November 1, 2026 at 12:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs secondary just got a lot thinner, but they're getting a key receiver back for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos. On offense, the news is about receiver Rashee Rice, who will be back in the lineup according to a report from Nate Taylor of ESPN. Rice will be returning from a hamstring injury he sustained against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. Rice was able to participate in every practice this week, per reports, and he currently has 13 receptions on 16 targets for 190 yards and a touchdown. As for the two cornerbacks, Delane is the more serious injury by far. The rookie was Kansas City's top draft choice with the No. 6 pick in the draft, and his shoulder has been an issue since OTAs. He wore a non-contact jersey for most of the summer, but Delane was able to get back on the field for the Chiefs' opener against the Denver Broncos, and he had a big interception in Kansas City's 31-10 romp. But Delane has been on and off the injury report for weeks now with this same issue, so the news isn't exactly surprising. What was surprising, though, was coach Andy Reid revealing that the injury was a hairline fracture of his scapula. His stat line at the moment includes 27 tackles, an interception and five passes defended in five games this season. Sneed's situation is very different. He returned to Kansas City during the summer after a failed stint with the Tennessee Titans. His injury designation was personal/knee, but the personal part of this is new if there's anything substantial to it. Sneed played well early, but he was badly exposed in Kansas City's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night. The Seahawks picked on Sneed for most of the night, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba especially had some strong moments against the former Chiefs star. The Chiefs have also signed cornerback Melvin Smith to the active roster from the practice squad, and they activated defensive end Tyreke Smith from the practice squad to the game-day roster. Kansas City is 5-1 going into Sunday's contest at Denver, which is 5-2. with the two teams battling for the lead in the AFC West.

home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Can they make it three wins on the year this week down in South Florida? Historically, playing against the Miami Dolphins on the road has been a tall task for the Patriots. The heat, plus struggles against a team that's either been very good or very bad, hasn't led to the best of results for New England. This year, however, should be a solid victory for the Patriots — despite the conditions. "We have to be conditioned," head coach Mike Vrabel said this week. "I think the better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win." That was against a Bears defense that's in Super Bowl conversations. Against a Miami defense that has struggled all year, the 24-year-old should have a comfortable day in the pocket, even if some starters at both offensive line and wide receiver aren't playing. The New England Patriots have several roster needs ahead of the NFL trade deadline. But one writer believes the team should avoid making a major investment in weapons for quarterback Drake Maye . NBC Sports Boston's Michael Hurley argued Monday, Nov. 2, that the Patriots should take wide receiver off their list of potential trade targets, despite injuries to A.J. Brown , Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs . Hurley's call comes with New England sitting at 5-3 following Sunday's 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins . Patriots Advised Against Bringing in Wide Receiver Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK – OCTOBER 04: Head coach Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots congratulates Romeo Doubs #87 after a touchdown against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter at Highmark Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Hurley ranked the Patriots' biggest trade deadline needs on Monday, placing wide receiver completely outside his top five. The position has drawn attention because of injuries to Brown, Hollins and Doubs, who have all missed multiple games this season. But Hurley asserted that the Patriots have committed a great deal of resources to their receiving corps, making one more acquisition hard to justify. "Throwing more draft picks at that one position right now would be unwise," Hurley wrote. The Patriots signed Doubs to a four-year, $68 million contract during the offseason, including $39 million guaranteed. New England subsequently acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for first- and fifth-round draft picks. Brown is earning $29 million this season, according to Hurley. Hurley also pointed toward the returns of their injured players as grounds to exercise patience. At the same time, Maye demonstrated that New England can still generate explosive plays without big dogs at receiver. The quarterback completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns against Miami, finding Kyle Williams for a 43-yard score and DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard touchdown. Brown with the New England Patriots this season. The Philadelphia Eagles traded him back in June for a 2027 fifth-rounder and a 2028 first-rounder. However, the wide receiver's debut in New England has been underwhelming. So far, Brown has missed four games this season due to an injury. He was activated on Oct. 17 and has played in the last two games. However, another concerning update has emerged. On Wednesday, after being listed on the injury report with a knee ailment, the Super Bowl LIX champion missed Thursday's practice session with the Patriots. Fans on social media shared their reactions to A.J. Brown's latest injury concern. "The Eagles fleeced them," a fan said. "Dude is made of glass.. Won't be drafting again," another fan wrote. "We tried to tell you he was washed," one fan commented . In the team's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain. Patriots WR coach Todd Downing shares his thoughts on A.J. Brown On Thursday, New England Patriots WR coach Todd Downing spoke with the media. While discussing A.J. Brown and his performance so far, Downing said that he has faith in the wide receiver despite his underwhelming showcase. "It's been a small sample size for A.J.," Downing said. "I think there's been a lot made about a couple of weeks. My hope, and his hope, and everybody hopes that he gets a little bit of traction. "I'm not worried about where A.J. is at all. On Friday, New England listed WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable for Week 8. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for the season due to a blood clot, putting Tanner McKee in the starting quarterback position for the foreseeable future. The Eagles have been banged up across the board this season, but especially on offense with DeVonta Smith (out in Week 8) and Saquon Barkley both missing time. That’s led to the Eagles ranking in the bottom five in the league in EPA/Play on offense, and it puts them as underdogs in this divisional matchup against the Commanders. Washington lost star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season in Week 6, but it's coming off a bye and still has a chance to make a play for the top spot in the NFC East. Daniels was dealing with a dislocated elbow, has played in the last two games – and played well – despite making a critical mistake in overtime in a tie against the New York Giants. If the Commanders don’t turn things around sooner rather than later, there’s a good chance Dan Quinn could be coaching for his job. All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections, and much more for this NFC East rivalry matchup. Philly has struggled a bit against the pass, ranking 28th in passing yards allowed, in the bottom 10 in passing touchdowns allowed and 25th in EPA/Pass. That’s a great sign for Jayden Daniels, who had his best game of the season throwing the ball in Week 6 against San Francisco. The star quarterback threw for 300 yards and completed 72.5 percent of his passes in a close loss in primetime. He had just 164 passing yards against Philly in Week 1, but Daniels has been much more effective since coming back from a dislocated elbow, combining for over 300 passing and rushing yards in back-to-back games. He’s worth a look on Sunday night with so many other star players banged up. Earlier this season, Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert had four catches for 77 yards and two scores in a Week 1 win over Washington. He has not found the end zone since, but the veteran tight end has remained a big part of the offense. Over the last two weeks with McKee at quarterback, Goedert has been targeted 15 times, catching 11 passes for 109 yards. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. The Week 8 battle of the NFC East basement pits the Philadelphia Eagles against the Washington Commanders (-5.5) on Sunday, Nov. 1. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but this one could go a long way toward defining the second half of the season. Here are my favorite NFL picks for tonight's game, led by the Over. TOP PICK Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with the Cowboys for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completion rate with two TDs in a loss to the 49ers on Oct. 19. With both defenses leaking, there should be plenty of points, and you'll find more totals ideas in our Week 8 Over/Under predictions . Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses, especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and has given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin , doing plenty of damage out of the slot. He burned the Eagles in his NFL debut and is projected for as many as 46 receiving yards in Week 8. Our Eagles vs. Commanders prop picks and Week 8 expert combo picks have more ways to attack this game. Dallas Goedert anytime touchdown Antonio Williams 30+ receiving yards Eagles vs Commanders touchdown scorer: Dallas Goedert With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks still hurting, tight end Goedert sees a spike in his involvement in the passing game. Goedert drew seven targets for five receptions in Week 7 and has been McKee's safety blanket during his two-game stint as the starter. The Eagles face a Commanders defense that has been bullied by rival tight ends this season. Washington ranks dead last in DVOA vs. tight ends, allowing the seventh most yards to the position along with eight touchdowns to TEs in just six games. Goedert is responsible for two of those touchdowns, with a pair of scores in the win over Washington in Week 1. His touchdown forecasts for this return matchup range from 19% to as high as 44%, with the majority at 30% or higher. See all of our Eagles vs. Commanders touchdown picks for more options. Eagles vs Commanders player prop: Antonio Williams 30+ receiving yards Terry McLaurin's injury has created a vacuum in the Washington pass game, shuffling around the healthy WRs. That's a commodity the Commies are running short on in Week 8. On top of McLaurin's season-ending injury, Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks are both on the injury report for SNF. That leaves rookie Antonio Williams in a good place, in terms of his work in the offense. His numbers have been good when Daniels is under center, with his worst yardage performances coming when the QB1 was injured. Head coach Dan Quinn told the media he was thrilled with Williams' development and Football IQ, following a 50-yard outing in Week 6. Williams has carved out a spot as Washington's top slot option, playing the inside position on almost half his snaps. That matches up well against Philadelphia, which has struggled to contain slot receivers this season. Williams caught all four balls his way for 64 yards and a touchdown in his pro debut versus the Eagles in Week 1. His Week 8 projections all sit north of 30 yards with a ceiling of 46+. away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night. Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening. Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset? How to watch Seahawks vs. Bears live Date: Monday, Nov. 2 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lumen Field (Seattle) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -3, O/U 46.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests. For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores. Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league. The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground. The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box. The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year. When the Seahawks have the ball Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's . Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual. The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions. Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head. Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.) The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league. Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home. away.headline: Kyle Monangai a nonparticipant on estimated injury report, leaving Chicago Bears RB’s Week 8 status in doubt
away.blurb: Monangai is listed with thumb and toe injuries, but the toe issue has kept him out of the last three games. Meanwhile, Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad II, who left the Week 7 win against the New England Patriots in the third quarter, was limited with a toe injury in the estimated report. D’Marco Jackson (ankle) also was limited, while fellow linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion) were designated as full participants. home.headline: Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without at least three players for Monday night's game against the Bears, with left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) all ruled out due to injury. Additionally, outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is doubtful due to an ankle injury that kept him off the practice field all week. On a positive note, running back Zach Charbonnet does not have a game status and head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Charbonnet will play Monday, marking his return from a torn ACL suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs. Four players are questionable for the Seahawks, guard Anthony Bradford (knee), quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow), linebacker Patrick O'Connell (toe) and defensive tackle Brandon Pili (back) For the Bears, Kyle Monangai, the team's second-leading rusher, is out due to thumb and toe injuries. Linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe) are questionable. Several players who were limited on Thursday were upgraded to full participation on Friday, including running back Jadarian Price , who is eligible to return from injured reserve this week. In addition to Price, those going from limited to full participation were outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf), linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (Achilles). Guard Anthony Bradford (knee), went from limited Thursday to not participating Friday, running back Zach Charbonnet went from full Thursday to limited on Friday, and linebacker Patrick O'Connell (toe) went from limited to not participating. For the Bears, tight end Colston Loveland was a new addition to the report, listed as limited due to a neck injury. The only other change from Thursday's report was linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) going from limited a day earlier to not practicing on Friday. Ten players were listed as limited, though in the case of veteran outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence, it was for rest. New to the injury report this week is defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who was limited with an Achilles injury. home.headline: Seahawks’ Week 8 injury report vs. Bears: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price set to return for MNF clash
home.blurb: Seahawks’ Week 8 injury report vs. Bears: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price set to return for MNF clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Alex House, ClutchPoints Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:08 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It is quite easy to blame the Seattle Seahawks ' uneven first half on an inefficient run game, but the defending Super Bowl champions did not exactly post eye-popping numbers on the ground during the 2025 regular season. They averaged 4.1 yards per carry and ranked 11th in the league with 123.3 rushing yards per week. Though, even when the backfield was lacking firepower, it still posed a threat to defenses. The 2026 Seahawks are hoping to get that back on Monday. Emanuel Wilson has done his best to shoulder the burden following Kenneth Walker III's free-agency departure and multiple injuries to the position group, eclipsing 80 rushing yards on three separate occasions. He can use some help, though. An incoming future Hall of Fame offensive lineman like Quenton Nelson should provide a huge boost , but a versatile RB room is an important element of many successful teams. And Seattle (4-3) is ready to shake things up a bit. Zach Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut versus the Chicago Bears , and although he is still on injured reserve at time of print, rookie Jadarian Price is in line to join him. The former is returning from a torn ACL he suffered in the playoffs back in January, and the latter logged full practice participation on Friday after missing the last month of action with a chest injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bears are inserting All-Pro defensive tackle and big midseason acquisition Jeffery Simmons into their front seven, so the Seahawks may have a better chance of keeping Chicago on its toes with their top-three ball-carriers. Fans have seen what quarterback Sam Darnold can accomplish when Seattle establishes its ground attack. Even without Kyle Monangai, who is still battling turf toe and a thumb injury, the Bears boast a dangerous D'Andre Swift-led rushing unit. The Seahawks must close the gap in that crucial area on Monday night. Their chances of doing so have seemingly improved. Opening kickoff will commence at 8:15 p.m. ET.
