home.blurb: Seahawks-Bears injury report: Cross and Shaheed out, ‘Big Cat’ limited with Achilles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Seattle Seahawks have a lengthy injury report to start their prep for the showdown with the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football with a whopping 18(!!) players listed with some sort of designation. The DNP's for injury included Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed, and Uchenna Nwosu. Notable limited participants were Tyrice Knight, Drake Thomas, the newly-returning Jadarian Price, and Leonard Williams who popped up with an Achilles injury…maybe I shouldn't have used the word "popped" in his case. Find some wood to knock on if you're superstitious. As this is the first injury report of the week, we'll need to see how things shake out over the next few days to see who is really in danger of missing the primetime game. Ted Zahn Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:32 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads New Seahawks Quenton Nelson was listed as a full participant along with Zach Charbonnet. The hope is that both of them along with potentially Jadarian Price will help take the run game to another level, thus lessening the load on Sam Darnold's shoulders. Mike Macdonald seemed relatively positive about Cross, saying that IR wasn't in consideration at this time. The less time he misses, the more he'll get to gel with his new partner in crime on the left side in Nelson.

home.headline: FINAL Bears vs Seahawks Injury Reports: Updates on Monangai, Charbonnet, Shaheed, Loveland & More
home.blurb: MLB Probable Pitchers & Starting Lineups MLB Odds Public Betting Props Probable Pitchers & Lineups Weather Reports ATS Records Futures News Seattle enters banged up on both sides of the ball, officially ruling out starting left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), and running back Velus Jones Jr (hamstring). Chicago's injury report is cleaner, though running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) has been ruled out, and linebackers D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and defensive back Malik Muhammad II (toe) carry questionable designations into kickoff. Kyle Monangai (RB) The most impactful confirmed absence for Chicago is running back Kyle Monangai. He failed to practice this week and is officially out with a thumb injury. His absence dramatically shifts the ground and pound workload in the backfield. In the three games Monangai has missed this season, starting running back D'Andre Swift has averaged 55 rushing yards. D'Marco Jackson (LB) & The Linebacker Corps The Chicago defense appeared to be walking on eggshells with several key linebackers hitting the report, but the outlook is largely positive. D'Marco Jackson is listed as questionable with an ankle injury, though he managed to log a full practice. Drew Lock (QB) & Sam Darnold Backup quarterback Drew Lock was limited in practice due to an elbow injury and heads into the game carrying a questionable tag. Velus Jones Jr (RB) & The Backfield Carousel The Seattle rushing attack takes a confirmed hit with running back Velus Jones Jr ruled out due to a hamstring injury. However, his absence creates a fascinating betting angle for backup running back Emanuel Wilson. In the one game Jones missed earlier this season, Wilson erupted for an average of 92 rushing yards. Despite this historical production, best-available odds have Wilson's rushing yards total set incredibly low at just 19.5 yards. That's because fellow running back Zach Charbonnet managed a full practice and is expected to play for the first time this season with his prop sitting at 32.5 rushing yards. Rookie RB Jadarian Price is also expected to be activated off injured reserve, further muddying the waters for how the carries will be divvied out. Uchenna Nwosu (LB) & The Defensive Front On the defensive side of the ball, standout linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is listed as doubtful with an ankle injury. The Seattle linebacker corps is heavily featured on the report, with Patrick O'Connell questionable.
